claim: The number of children born since the origin of Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) exceeds 5 million.
source: the number of children born to date using these methods exceeds 5 million (International Committee for Monitoring Assisted Reproductive Technology I, 2012)
evidence: Supported by citation to International Committee for Monitoring Assisted Reproductive Technology I, 2012

claim: A higher frequency of defects has been reported among ART-conceived infants.
source: The majority seem healthy, but a higher frequency of defects has been reported among ART-conceived infants, suggesting an epigenetic cost.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a general observation from the literature

claim: This study reports the first whole-genome DNA methylation datasets from single pig blastocysts showing differences between in vivo and in vitro produced embryos.
source: We report the first whole-genome DNA methylation datasets from single pig blastocysts showing differences between in vivo and in vitro produced embryos.
evidence: Direct statement of the study's novel contribution

claim: Natur-IVF embryos were of higher quality than C-IVF in terms of cell number and hatching ability.
source: Natur-IVF embryos were of higher quality than C-IVF in terms of cell number and hatching ability.
evidence: Stated in abstract and supported by data in Table 2

claim: Natur-IVF embryos have expression and methylation patterns closer to in vivo blastocysts than C-IVF embryos.
source: RNA-Seq and DNA methylation analyses showed that Natur-IVF embryos have expression and methylation patterns closer to in vivo blastocysts.
evidence: Stated in abstract and supported by RNA-Seq and DNA methylation data presented in the results

claim: Genes involved in reprogramming, imprinting and development were affected by culture, with fewer aberrations in Natur-IVF embryos.
source: Genes involved in reprogramming, imprinting and development were affected by culture, with fewer aberrations in Natur-IVF embryos.
evidence: Stated in abstract and supported by gene expression analysis in results

claim: Methylation analysis detected methylated changes in C-IVF, but not in Natur-IVF, at genes whose methylation could be critical, such as IGF2R and NNAT.
source: Methylation analysis detected methylated changes in C-IVF, but not in Natur-IVF, at genes whose methylation could be critical, such as IGF2R and NNAT.
evidence: Stated in abstract and supported by methylation data in Figure 7 and Figure 8

claim: Infertility affects 20% of couples according to a WHO study in 190 countries.
source: In humans, according to a study by the World Health Organisation (WHO) in 190 countries, infertility affects 20% of couples and it was estimated that at least 40.5 million women were seeking infertility medical care in 2007 (Mascarenhas et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Mascarenhas et al., 2012

claim: Studies have reported higher rates of preterm births in ART pregnancies.
source: Although the majority of them seem healthy, studies have reported higher rates of preterm births (Rubens et al., 2014), non-chromosomal birth defects and adverse perinatal effects in ART pregnancies (El Hajj and Haaf, 2013)
evidence: Supported by citations to Rubens et al., 2014 and El Hajj and Haaf, 2013

claim: Swine could be a good candidate for modeling ART-related disorders in humans due to their genetic, anatomical and physiological similarities with humans.
source: For modeling ART-related disorders in human, swine could be a good candidate for several reasons: their genetic, anatomical and physiological similarities with human (Swindle et al., 2012); their size and length of gestation; and the availability of individuals genetically selected by their excellent reproductive performance in artificial insemination centres.
evidence: Supported by citation to Swindle et al., 2012 and reasoning about pig characteristics

claim: Spermatozoa selected by swim-up show higher rates of normal morphology and motility, and decreased DNA fragmentation and methylation levels.
source: Since it was observed that spermatozoa selected by swim-up show higher rates of normal morphology and motility, and decreased DNA fragmentation and methylation levels (Kim et al., 2015)
evidence: Supported by citation to Kim et al., 2015

claim: The embryo is sensitive to its very early environment and culture media used in ART may have long-lasting consequences.
source: In both mouse and human, accumulating evidence indicates that the embryo is sensitive to its very early environment and that culture media used in ART (as factors involved in technique-derived effects) may have long-lasting consequences (Kleijkers et al., 2014; Fernandez-Gonzalez et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kleijkers et al., 2014 and Fernandez-Gonzalez et al., 2004

claim: The presence of serum in culture media has been linked to the incidence of Large Offspring syndrome (LOS) in ruminants.
source: Several imprinting disorders and abnormal phenotypes have been linked to ART, but of special significance is the relationship between the presence of serum in culture media and the incidence of Large Offspring syndrome (LOS) in ruminants (Young et al., 1998)
evidence: Supported by citation to Young et al., 1998

claim: More than 150 proteins have been described in the oviductal fluid.
source: the reproductive fluids have a different composition to serum and are extremely rich in proteins other than serum albumin (more than 150 have been described in the oviductal fluid [Avilés et al., 2010])
evidence: Supported by citation to Avilés et al., 2010

claim: Protein enrichment of media compared with addition of serum albumin alone improved the blastocyst implantation rate and may increase human births by more than 8%.
source: A similar conclusion can be reached from a clinical trial showing that protein enrichment of media compared with addition of serum albumin alone improved the blastocyst implantation rate and may increase human births by more than 8% (Meintjes et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Meintjes et al., 2009

claim: Single blastocyst whole-genome DNA methylation profiles comparing in vivo and in vitro produced embryos have not been published for any mammalian species prior to this study.
source: However, so far, single blastocyst whole-genome DNA methylation profiles comparing in vivo and in vitro produced embryos have not been published for any mammalian species and we therefore aim to produce these in this study.
evidence: Statement of novelty based on literature review

claim: Modified swim-up protocols for the selection of spermatozoa in pigs and the use of reproductive secretions as additives in the culture media significantly increase the yield and quality of the blastocysts produced.
source: We report here that modified swim-up protocols for the selection of spermatozoa in pigs and the use of reproductive secretions as additives in the culture media significantly increase the yield and quality of the blastocysts produced from a morphological, epigenetic and gene expression point of view.
evidence: Supported by experimental data presented in Tables 1 and 2, and RNA-Seq and methylation analyses

claim: Swim-up protocols obtained significantly higher rates of monospermy than conventional density gradient centrifugation (49.6 ± 4.5 vs 17.4 ± 4.1).
source: With these new protocols, we obtained significantly higher rates of monospermy than with conventional ones (49.6 ± 4.5 vs 17.4 ± 4.1, Table 1)
evidence: Supported by data in Table 1

claim: The final percentage of putative zygotes was significantly higher with swim-up protocols than with conventional density gradient centrifugation (35.2 ± 0.2 vs 14.6 ± 0.1).
source: the final percentage of putative zygotes (evaluated at 24 hours post insemination, hpi) was significantly higher (35.2 ± 0.2 vs 14.6 ± 0.1, Table 1)
evidence: Supported by data in Table 1

claim: The addition of POF-LF to the Swim-up media instead of BSA increased the final yield of the system (35.2 ± 0.2 vs 29.7 ± 0.2).
source: Moreover, the addition of POF-LF to the Swim-up media instead of BSA increased the final yield of the system (35.2 ± 0.2 vs 29.7 ± 0.2, Table 1).
evidence: Supported by data in Table 1

claim: More than 40% of cleaved embryos reached the blastocyst stage in both C-IVF and Natur-IVF groups.
source: Regarding embryo development, more than 40% of cleaved embryos reached the blastocyst stage in both groups (Table 2A).
evidence: Supported by data in Table 2A

claim: Natur-IVF blastocysts showed a significant increase in their mean number of cells (81.8 ± 7.2) compared to C-IVF blastocysts (49.9 ± 3.7).
source: However, the Natur-IVF blastocysts showed a significant increase in their mean number of cells (81.8 ± 7.2, Table 2A) compared to the C-IVF ones (49.9 ± 3.7)
evidence: Supported by data in Table 2A

claim: The mean number of cells in Natur-IVF blastocysts (81.8 ± 7.2) was similar to that observed in in vivo samples (87.0 ± 7.2).
source: this number was similar to that observed in the in vivo samples (In-vivo group, 87.0 ± 7.2)
evidence: Supported by data in Table 2A

claim: At day 7.5, embryos reaching the hatching or hatched stages were observed only in the Natur-IVF group.
source: Moreover, at day 7.5, embryos reaching the hatching or hatched stages were observed only in the Natur-IVF group (Table 2B).
evidence: Supported by data in Table 2B

claim: In vitro culture systems significantly alter embryonic gene expression as previously observed in pooled pig blastocysts.
source: In vitro culture systems significantly alter embryonic gene expression as previously observed in pooled pig blastocysts (Bauer et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bauer et al., 2010

claim: Mean number of raw reads was 14.24 ± 2.23 (±SD) millions for RNA-Seq libraries.
source: Mean number of raw reads was 14.24 ± 2.23 (±SD) millions
evidence: Direct statement of sequencing data quality metrics

claim: Transcripts from 13,309 to 14,512 different genes were detected in each individual blastocyst.
source: transcripts from 13,309 to 14,512 different genes (from a total of 20,789 annotated pig mRNAs) were detected in each individual
evidence: Direct statement of RNA-Seq detection results

claim: Principal Component Analysis showed that the three embryos from each group clustered together, with C-IVF embryos showing higher variability.
source: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) showed that, despite expected individual variability, the three embryos from each group clustered together (Figure 3B), with the C-IVF embryos showing higher variability
evidence: Supported by PCA plot in Figure 3B

claim: Natur-IVF was closer to the In vivo group (Pearson correlation coefficient r = 0.95) than C-IVF (r = 0.938).
source: Therefore, after combining the triplicates, data from both in vitro groups showed high correlation (Pearson correlation coefficient [r] = 0.964), but Natur-IVF was closer to the In vivo group ([r] = 0.95) than C-IVF ([r] = 0.938).
evidence: Direct statement of correlation analysis results

claim: RNA-Seq data analysis identified 787 differentially expressed genes between C-IVF and In-vivo.
source: RNA-Seq data analysis (DESeq2 p<0.05 after multiple testing correction) identified 787 differentially expressed genes (DEG) between the C-IVF and In-vivo
evidence: Direct statement of differential expression analysis results

claim: RNA-Seq data analysis identified 621 differentially expressed genes between Natur-IVF and In vivo.
source: 621 DEGs between Natur-IVF and In vivo (Figure 3—source data 1, including also all the expression values for all the genes)
evidence: Direct statement of differential expression analysis results

claim: There were 440 genes that showed aberrant expression only in C-IVF vs In vivo.
source: However, there were 440 genes (from the 784 DEGs in C-IVF) that showed aberrant expression only in C-IVF vs In vivo (DEGs only in C-IVF, Figure 3C)
evidence: Supported by Venn diagram in Figure 3C

claim: 281 genes showed aberrant expression only in the Natur-IVF group vs In vivo, which is 40% fewer than C-IVF.
source: while 40% fewer genes (n = 281 from the 620 DEGs in Natur-IVF) showed aberrant expression only in the Natur-IVF group vs In vivo (DEGs only in Natur-IVF, Figure 3C)
evidence: Supported by Venn diagram in Figure 3C and calculation

claim: Several genes related to epigenetic reprogramming (DNMT3B, DNMT1, HDAC5, KDM5A) were amongst the C-IVF-specific DEGs.
source: Importantly, several genes related to epigenetic reprogramming (down: DNMT3B, DNMT1; up: HDAC5, KDM5A), embryo development (down: CTGF, ING2, KIT, EZH2; up: BMP4, TLN1, ADAR), cell growth (down: CDCA5, SMC1A; up: RB1, SMARCA2) or imprinting (up: IGF2BP2, GNAS; down: DIRAS3) were amongst the C-IVF-specific DEGs (Figure 3D).
evidence: Supported by heatmap in Figure 3D

claim: Only 29 genes reached significant expression differences between the two in vitro groups after DESeq2 analysis.
source: Direct comparison between Natur-IVF vs In vivo and C-IVF vs In vivo DEGs revealed that only 29 genes reached significant expression differences between the two in vitro groups after DESeq2 analysis (Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: Direct statement of differential expression analysis results

claim: Of the 29 DEGs between in vitro groups, 13 were similarly expressed in Natur-IVF and In vivo, and only seven showed similar expression between C-IVF and In vivo groups.
source: Interestingly, of these 29 DEGs, 13 were similarly expressed in Natur-IVF and In vivo, and only seven showed similar expression between C-IVF and In vivo groups (Figure 3C, Figure 3—source data 2).
evidence: Direct statement of comparative analysis results

claim: The global methylation percentages of CpGs were 15.02 ± 3.3, 11.09 ± 2.6 and 12.33 ± 3.6 for the C-IVF, Natur-IVF and In-vivo groups, respectively.
source: The global methylation percentages of CpGs were 15.02 ± 3.3, 11.09 ± 2.6 and 12.33 ± 3.6 for the C-IVF, Natur-IVF and In-vivo groups, respectively.
evidence: Direct statement of methylation analysis results

claim: The generally low level of methylation suggests that the genome has experienced substantial loss of methylation from the gametes, analogous to that observed in other mammals.
source: The generally low level of methylation suggests that the genome has experienced substantial loss of methylation from the gametes, analogous to that observed in other mammals (Guo et al., 2014; Kobayashi et al., 2012).
evidence: Inference from methylation data supported by citations to Guo et al., 2014 and Kobayashi et al., 2012

claim: Fewer DMRs showed higher methylation in In vivo vs Natur-IVF (n = 1,660) than in In vivo vs C-IVF (n = 2244).
source: Globally, fewer DMRs showed higher methylation in In vivo vs Natur-IVF (n = 1,660) than in In vivo vs C-IVF (n = 2244) (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by Venn diagram in Figure 5B

claim: A DMR overlapping IGF2R was found in the subset of exclusive C-IVF DMRs.
source: A DMR overlapping IGF2R, a gene directly related with the LOS in ruminants and mouse, was found in the subset of exclusive C-IVF DMRs (Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: Direct statement of DMR analysis results

claim: The methylation percentages for the IGF2R region (Chr1: 9,199,522–9,201,143) were 12.45%, 28.3% and 35.5% for C-IVF, Natur-IVF and In vivo, respectively.
source: The methylation percentages for this region (Chr1: 9,199,522–9,201,143) were 12.45%, 28.3% and 35.5% for C-IVF, Natur-IVF and In vivo, respectively (Figure 7A).
evidence: Supported by data in Figure 7A

claim: A CpG island overlapping the IGF2R DMR showed significant differences in methylation (p<0.05): 14.1%, 27.8% and 29.4% for C-IVF, Natur-IVF and In vivo groups, respectively.
source: In addition, a CpG island (oe = 0.89, Chr1:9,200,658–9,202,276) that overlapped the DMR showed significant differences in methylation (p<0.05): 14.1%, 27.8% and 29.4% for C-IVF, Natur-IVF and In vivo groups, respectively (Figure 7B)
evidence: Supported by data in Figure 7B

claim: Comparison of methylation in the three groups of blastocysts for 14 candidate igDMRs revealed differences for ZAC1 and PEG10, which were more methylated (p<0.05) in the C-IVF than in In vivo group.
source: Comparison of methylation in the three groups of blastocysts for the resulting 14 candidate igDMRs (with sufficient read coverage) revealed differences for ZAC1 and PEG10, which were more methylated (p<0.05) in the C-IVF than in In vivo group
evidence: Direct statement of targeted methylation analysis results

claim: PEG10 and NNAT were more methylated (p<0.05) in the C-IVF than in Natur-IVF and In vivo groups.
source: PEG10 and NNAT, which were more methylated (p<0.05) in the C-IVF than in Natur-IVF and In vivo groups (Table 4B)
evidence: Supported by data in Table 4B

claim: No statistical differences in imprinted gene methylation were found between Natur-IVF and In vivo groups.
source: No statistical differences were found between Natur-IVF and In vivo groups.

claim: Knock-out mice lacking PEG10 showed early embryonic lethality with placental defects.
source: Knock-out mice lacking PEG10 showed early embryonic lethality with placental defects, indicating the importance of this gene in embryonic development (Ono et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ono et al., 2006

claim: The protein encoded by NNAT may be involved in the regulation of ion channels during brain development and may also play a role in forming and maintaining the structure of the nervous system.
source: The protein encoded by NNAT, on the other hand, may be involved in the regulation of ion channels during brain development and may also play a role in forming and maintaining the structure of the nervous system.

claim: Defects in methylation at ZAC1 and IGF2R have been found in patients with imprinted disorders including those born following the use of ART.
source: Defects in methylation at ZAC1 and IGF2R have been found in patients with the imprinted disorders transient neonatal diabetes mellitus (TNDM) or Silver-Russell syndrome (SRS), respectively, including those born following the use of ART (Le Bouc et al., 2010).

claim: CDKN1A inhibits embryonic cell proliferation in response to DNA damage and is considered one of the key genes responsible for the abnormalities in ART embryos.
source: CDKN1A inhibits embryonic cell proliferation in response to DNA damage and it is considered one of the key genes responsible for the abnormalities in ART embryos since an aberrant increase of CDKN1A expression might be related to the growth-defect phenotype (Ishimura et al., 2016).

claim: SLC2A3 (Glut-3) and SLC2A2 have been related to LOS and were highly up-regulated in the two in vitro groups.
source: The same situation was found for SLC2A3 (Glut-3) and SLC2A2, which have been related to LOS (Wrenzycki et al., 2004) and were highly up-regulated in the two in vitro groups.
evidence: Supported by citation to Wrenzycki et al., 2004 and gene expression data

claim: The exclusive alteration in C-IVF of genes such as KIT, UBR2, and ISOC1 supports the hypothesis that offspring produced with Natur-IVF conditions would be healthier than those produced with C-IVF.
source: Finally, the exclusive alteration in C-IVF of genes such as KIT, whose knock-out in mouse results in multiple alterations including embryonic lethality (Ro et al., 2010), UBR2, whose deletion results in female embryonic lethality and growth arrest (Kwon et al., 2003), or ISOC1, whose mutation produces phenotypes with body weight loss (Rainger et al., 2013), support the hypothesis that offspring produced with Natur-IVF conditions would be healthier than those produced with C-IVF, although additional studies are necessary to confirm this finding.
evidence: Inference based on gene expression data and citations to Ro et al., 2010; Kwon et al., 2003; Rainger et al., 2013

claim: This study represents the first time genome-wide DNA methylation and transcription analysis in single blastocysts (in vivo and in vitro) of a mammalian species.
